title: Less is Moore
summary: A Moore graph simultaneously asks for two things that normally pull in opposite directions: every vertex should have many neighbors, while every pair of vertices should remain close. For diameter two and degree $k$, the Moore bound is $k^2+1$, and equality forces a remarkably rigid graph: it is strongly regular with parameters $(k^2+1,k,0,1)$. Hoffman and Singleton showed that such a graph can exist only for $k=2,3,7$, and possibly 57. The degree-57 case on 3,250 vertices remains open.
